Mortality rate is a critical metric for evaluating the outcomes of patients diagnosed with [[atrieflimren|atrieflimren]] in [[danmark|Danmark]]. Data from the [[databasen-for-atrieflimren-i-danmark|Databasen for Atrieflimren i Danmark]] tracks both short-term and long-term survival across the country's healthcare regions, providing a comprehensive view of patient outcomes over time.

Historically, the database reported that 10% of all patients with atrial fibrillation in Denmark died during the reporting period [^src1]. More recent data covering the period from July 1, 2023, to June 30, 2024, indicates that the mortality rate for prevalent patients with atrial fibrillation was 7.3% at the national level [^src2]. Furthermore, the proportion of newly diagnosed patients who die within one year of their diagnosis was recorded at 12.5% [^src2]. 

When looking at broader national statistics, the proportion of prevalent patients who died during the reporting period was 7.6% nationwide [^src3]. There is a slight regional variation in these outcomes. Across the five Danish regions—[[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]], [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]], [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]], [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]], and [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]]—mortality rates for prevalent patients varied between 7.4% and 7.9% [^src3]. Similarly, the one-year mortality rate following diagnosis was 13.1% nationally, with regional variations ranging from 12.6% to 14.1% [^src3].
